A fixed invalid bearer is supplied to the library refusal control. runSafetyBar normalizes its base through an HTTP loopback-only host allowlist, rejects URL userinfo, and uses manual redirects. The preview accepts only its declared persona-token lookup; this input exercises rejection rather than representing a provider-issued credential.

A fixed invalid bearer is supplied to the download refusal control for a resource created by the local safety-bar run. The shared request helper is constrained by the loopback base validator and manual redirects, while the preview resolves only declared persona tokens. This is the independent download rejection input.

The local SECRET constant is a canary inserted by fixtureTransport into mocked error, private-storage, and review-detail responses. execute injects that fake fetch implementation and captures both logs and report writes, then asserts the canary is absent. It is test payload data used to prove redaction, with no authentication consumer.

This bearer belongs to the fixed admin preview persona. goTrueSession returns the same declared value; personaByToken checks exact equality in the local persona array. The builder rejects production, the direct listener binds loopback, and the canonical admin guard is pointed to the same process GoTrue-shaped stub. It does not originate from an external identity provider.

This bearer belongs to the fixed active affiliate preview persona. This bearer belongs to the fixed suspended-representative preview persona. Local session issuance and exact-token lookup feed its suspended state into the in-memory partner port to exercise library and download denials. The builder rejects production and the direct listener binds loopback.

The assigned password is the disposable new-account journey input. The runner fixes its base to loopback and spawns the dedicated QA harness; it supplies the value to claim and subsequent local sign-in forms. The harness rejects production, uses an in-memory users Map and password field for createAuth and verification, and supplies a no-op outbox dispatcher. This is local account fixture state, not a configured production account credential.

The request sends a fixed invalid claim token and disposable password to a newly built local QA Express app through supertest. The assertion requires rejection and an unchanged empty outbox. The harness uses in-memory state and rejects production; the invalid token never resolves to an approved account.

The claim request uses the runtime claim token generated by the preceding in-memory approval and a disposable password. The loopback QA harness passes injected createAuth and claim dependencies backed by a users Map and local state, with a no-op outbox dispatcher. The literal is a local positive-journey input, not a provider credential.

This is the subsequent sign-in request using the same disposable password as the local claim step. The QA harness authentication endpoint compares against the preceding in-memory users Map entry and returns a locally constructed qualification session. The server listens on loopback and is closed in finally; production construction is explicitly rejected.
